clue.text: Piano piece — a very small one

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an article is a piece of writing in a newspaper or a single item

explanation.surface: A music lover asks for a tiny piano composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano piece' reads as a single musical work, but it splits into a one-letter abbreviation and a word for a written item.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute fragment of matter, the smallest of bits.

clue.text: Where an adder slides to and fro?

definitions.text: Where an adder slides to and fro?

parts.words: Where an adder slides to and fro?
parts.note: the snake picture is false: an adder here is a person doing sums, sliding beads back and forth on wires

explanation.surface: A venomous snake slithering back and forth in some favourite spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' pretends to be the snake; it is someone who adds up figures, moving counters along rods.
explanation.definitionFit: A counting frame is worked by sliding beads along rods to add figures.

clue.text: Expressions of gratitude and disapproval are forbidden

parts.note: ta is an informal British way of saying thanks
boo is the noise a crowd makes to show disapproval

explanation.surface: Saying thank you and jeering are both banned in some strict setting.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited by custom or rule is said to be off-limits, a social ban.

clue.text: Sort of paper-round?

definitions.meaning: a thick, tough drawing paper used by artists
a single round of ammunition for a gun

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of newspaper delivery route this is.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins 'paper-round' into a newsagent's delivery job, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drawing paper bears this name, and so does a single shell or bullet loaded into a firearm.

clue.text: Its lace may be used in many undergarments

definitions.text: Its lace may be used in many undergarments

indicators.note: the letters of the words its lace may be put to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Its lace may be used in many undergarments: a remark about lingerie trimmings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be used' signals that ITS LACE is rearranged; the whole clue also describes the stretchy material found in waistbands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy cord or tape is sewn into waistbands of knickers and pants to keep them up.

clue.text: Two-foot tropical tree

indicators.note: two signals that the word for foot is written out twice in a row

parts.note: a paw is an animal's foot

explanation.surface: A tropical tree is described as having two feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-foot' looks like a measurement of height, but it asks for an animal's foot written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya plant of warm climates goes by this alternative name.

clue.text: Drink up with mother in holiday resort

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
ma is an informal name for mother

explanation.surface: Finishing a drink with Mum on holiday at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LAP to give PAL. 'Drink up' reads as an order to finish a glass. PALMA is the capital of Majorca, a popular Spanish island destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The Majorcan capital is a well-known Mediterranean beach destination.

clue.text: Canned — as sardines are

definitions.meaning: tinned sardines are packed thoroughly in oil

explanation.surface: Tinned, like sardines in a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like it means tinned, matching the sardines, but its first sense is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for thoroughly drunk, and literally describing fish soaked in plenty of oil.

clue.text: From the old gardener's chest came material for his mate

definitions.text: From the old gardener's chest came material for his mate

parts.words: From the old gardener's chest came material for his mate
parts.note: the first man, who tended Eden, gave up a bone from his chest from which his wife was made

explanation.surface: Something taken from an elderly gardener's trunk was used to make something for his friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old gardener' is the biblical first man, placed in the Garden of Eden; 'chest' is his ribcage, not a box, and 'mate' is his wife Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Eve was created from a bone taken from the side of the first man.

clue.text: Say a lot for one who gives inoculations

definitions.meaning: to talk rapidly and at length
someone who administers jabs, that is injections

explanation.surface: Asking what to call a chatty vaccinator.
explanation.walkthrough: JAB is British slang for an injection, so the second sense is a jocular coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter fast and incessantly; also, jocularly, a person who administers shots.

clue.text: No-one doubts what this signal means

definitions.text: No-one doubts what this signal means

parts.words: No-one doubts what this signal means
parts.note: the signal that danger is over is one whose meaning is plain to everybody

explanation.surface: A signal whose meaning is beyond any doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: it is the siren that marks the end of an air raid, and it says the meaning is plain to all.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal that a danger has passed, and literally 'understood by everyone'.

clue.text: His word is law at a court perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of at a court might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A judge whose rulings in court are law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AT A COURT; the court setting suggests a judge, but the definition describes an absolute ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot rules with unchecked power, so whatever he says must be obeyed.

clue.text: Nothing in a trick to alarm

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the word for trick

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or ploy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A harmless prank meant to frighten someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside RUSE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to stir or startle them, a sense close to waking them up.

clue.text: A sign of education in a reactionary Siamese, we hear

parts.note: old school describes traditional, conservative attitudes

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is replaced by another that sounds the same

parts.note: Siam is the old name for Thailand, so a Siamese person is Thai

explanation.surface: A conservative Siamese person showing signs of good schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns THAI into its sound-alike TIE. The neckwear of a British public school marks a privileged education.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie in a former pupil's school colours displays where they were educated.

clue.text: No longer in the cast, but in touch

definitions.meaning: an actor who has left a production is no longer in the show
in football or rugby a ball in touch has crossed the sideline

explanation.surface: An actor who has left the cast but keeps in touch with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in touch' looks like keeping in contact; in rugby and football touch is the area beyond the sidelines, where the ball is dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropped from a theatrical production, and also describing a ball that has left the field of play.

clue.text: How you may live if single-minded?

definitions.text: How you may live if single-minded?

parts.words: How you may live if single-minded?
parts.note: single-minded is reread as minded to be single, wanting to live alone

explanation.surface: A question about how a determined, focused person lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single-minded' usually means determined; here it means preferring the single life, so you live alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Living alone, without a partner or companions.

clue.text: Criminal making final bid to get outside

indicators.note: the word for bid is to get outside the word for final, wrapping round it

parts.note: an offer is a bid at an auction
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A crook making a last-ditch attempt to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final bid to get outside' reads as an escape plan; the bid is OFFER, which goes around END.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker is someone who commits an offence.

clue.text: Not to be found in a minute

definitions.text: Not to be found in a minute

parts.words: Not to be found in a minute
parts.note: minute here means the written minutes of a meeting, not sixty seconds, and remarks kept out of them are unrecorded

explanation.surface: Something that cannot be located quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' suggests a short time; it is the official written note of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made unofficially are not for publication or the formal record.

clue.text: Oriental art seen in new composition

indicators.note: a new composition of the letters art seen means they are put together in a different order

explanation.surface: Asian art displayed in a newly created work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new composition' rearranges ART SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and this word both describe things from Asia, the lands to the east.

clue.text: American beauty queen is married

parts.note: the pageant winner from the States, once wed, is no longer a Miss; her title is read as a word for a wife

explanation.surface: News that the reigning US pageant winner has wed.
explanation.walkthrough: The title Miss US, said as one word, becomes the informal term for a wife, so the queen is married by her own name.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a wife, particularly one's own.

clue.text: Reinforce complaint that's raised

parts.note: a beef is slang for a grievance or complaint
something raised is up

explanation.surface: A grievance that has been raised needs strengthening.
explanation.walkthrough: BEEF is informal for a gripe, as in 'what's your beef?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen or bolster something by adding substance.

clue.text: Coming before a superior

definitions.meaning: the head of a religious house, such as a monastery

explanation.surface: Arriving ahead of someone more senior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' is the noun for the head of a religious community, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier in time; also the monk ranking just below an abbot.

clue.text: Animal disinfectant mixed deep inside the vessel

indicators.note: inside places the shuffled letters within the word for vessel

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

indicators.note: mixed signals the letters of deep are jumbled

explanation.surface: A disinfectant stirred deep into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns DEEP into EEPD, and 'inside' puts it within SHIP. It is the chemical bath farmers drive flocks through.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers plunge their flocks into a chemical wash to kill parasites in the fleece.

clue.text: Be under professional examination

indicators.note: under in a down clue means the second word comes below the first

parts.note: pro is short for professional
taken as written

explanation.surface: Undergoing a formal assessment by an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts BE beneath PRO in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough investigation or inquiry.

clue.text: City set within a river

indicators.note: within puts the word for set inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
laid means set down, placed

explanation.surface: A city located inside a river's course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts LAID inside DEE, after A. The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland; ADELAIDE is the capital of South Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital of South Australia.

clue.text: A player — one in new boots

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the reordered letters
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of boots

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A footballer wearing new boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BOOTS to OBOST and 'in' puts I inside it. 'player' suggests a sportsman in boots, but it is a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the reed instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: The plea and the pleader

definitions.meaning: an appeal or request made earnestly
one who prays, with the word read as pray plus er

explanation.surface: Both the request and the person making it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a jocular reading: one who prays.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest request to God; also, playfully, the person making that request.

clue.text: Negative poles seen to change? Absurd!

parts.note: no is a negative answer
N for the north pole
S for the south pole

indicators.note: to change means the letters of seen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Magnetic poles that switch around baffle a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges SEEN to ENSE. 'Negative poles' looks like a magnetism term, but splits into NO and two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief dismissing something as rubbish.
